summary: Tested new Lightbox + Traditions features on Argelia QR landing page. Most pass: nav link 'TRADICIONES' renders and scrolls; traditions-section visible with all 6 tradition-card-0..5 testids; clicking Karakou opens lightbox with correct title/subtitle and the prev/next/thumb buttons are correctly hidden when photos.length === 1; Escape key closes the lightbox; FR translation 'Traditions & Vêtements' and EN 'Traditions & Attire' both render; landscape-card-0 opens lightbox titled 'Tassili'. CRITICAL BUG: clicking the lightbox-close (X) button is intercepted by the fixed Navigation header — Playwright confirms 'main-navigation intercepts pointer events' on the close button. RCA: <Lightbox /> is rendered inside <main className='relative z-10'> which creates a stacking context, so its z-[80] is bounded by main's z-10 in the App scope; Navigation is a sibling of <main> at z-50, so it visually sits ABOVE the entire lightbox (including the close button area at top-right). Escape still closes it, but the X button is unclickable in the top region. NOTE: also verified Chedda (card 2) and Burnous (card 3) lightboxes — since clicking them ALSO opens the lightbox (which works), but I could not close them via X. Used Escape to close in fallback flow and confirmed 'Sin imagen disponible' fallback shows in both. Earlier iteration_1 features (history, people-modal, gastronomy, mobile menu, language switcher) were not re-checked end-to-end because the test halted on the lightbox-close timeout, but Karakou->Chedda->Burnous->Tassili opening flow + FR/EN translations + nav all confirmed working.

ui_bugs.issue: lightbox-close (X) button is intercepted by fixed Navigation header — header sits above lightbox visually so user cannot click X. Escape key still works.

issues: Navigation header is fully visible on top of the dark lightbox backdrop — should be hidden or covered when lightbox is open for a true fullscreen viewer experience.

action_items: Fix Lightbox z-index/stacking: render <Lightbox /> via React Portal to document.body (createPortal), OR move <Lightbox /> mounts out of <main className='relative z-10'> (e.g., as a sibling of Navigation in App.js), OR raise Navigation z-index ONLY when no lightbox is open and explicitly hide nav while lightbox.open === true. Recommended fix: createPortal in Lightbox.jsx — return createPortal(<AnimatePresence>...</AnimatePresence>, document.body). This guarantees the lightbox escapes any parent stacking context and the close button receives clicks.
Consider hiding the Navigation header (or setting pointer-events:none) while a lightbox is open to give a clean fullscreen viewer.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js: <main className='relative z-10'> creates a stacking context that traps the Lightbox's z-[80] below sibling fixed elements like Navigation (z-50). This is the root cause of the unclickable close button.

The bug to verify after fix: clicking [data-testid='lightbox-close'] should close the lightbox without timing out (currently nav header intercepts pointer events). rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: <main className='relative z-10'> in App.js wraps <Landscapes/> and <Traditions/>, both of which mount <Lightbox/> as children. CSS spec: a positioned element with z-index creates a stacking context that confines descendants. Therefore the Lightbox's z-[80] is INTERNAL to main's z-10 stacking context; from the App's perspective the entire lightbox renders at effective z-10. Meanwhile <Navigation/> is a sibling of <main> with fixed positioning and z-50, so it stacks above z-10, hence above the lightbox. REPRODUCE: open lightbox via any tradition or landscape card → try to click the X at top-right → Playwright reports 'main-navigation intercepts pointer events'. MITIGATION (preferred): use React portal — `import { createPortal } from 'react-dom'; return createPortal(<AnimatePresence>...</AnimatePresence>, document.body);` at the top of the Lightbox return. This detaches the lightbox from main's stacking context so its z-[80] competes at the document root level and wins over Navigation's z-50.
